commercial_refrigeration-cold__freezer_r.description:
Cold rooms are the ideal chilled storage solution for commercial environments where chest/counter refrigeration no longer provides enough storage space.

When it comes to cold rooms, you have a choice of refrigeration unit; Integral or Remote .

Which type of refrigeration unit you need will depend on the environment in which you intend on building your cold room.

Remote Refrigeration Units:

•Compressor is located away from the cold room unit and connected by pipes.

•Ideal for hot or confined spaces where ventilation is limited such as a commercial kitchen.

•Considered the most popular and reliable refrigeration system.

•Usually more efficient than the integral units.

•More complex install, specialist engineer required.

Integral Refrigeration Units:

•Lower initial capital cost than remote systems.

•Units can be either wall (straddle) or ceiling mounted.

•Ideal for well ventilated areas.

•recommended for use in environments of up to 32ºC ambient.

If you're not sure which refrigeration system would be right for you, give our sales team a call on 01229 480001 for some friendly and helpful advice on our wide range of cold rooms.

commercial_refrigeration-cold__freezer_r.description:
Cold rooms are the ideal chilled storage solution for commercial environments where chest/counter refrigeration no longer provides enough storage space.

If you're not sure whether an integral refrigeration unit is right for you, give our sales team a call on 01229 48000 for some friendly and helpful advice on our wide range of cold rooms.

Cold rooms are the ideal chilled storage solution for commercial environments where chest/counter refrigeration no longer provides enough storage space.

Remote refrigeration units are considered to be the most reliable , and the most popular option of refrigeration units when it comes to cold rooms. They are ideal where integral units are not; in hot or confined spaces where ventilation is limited such as a commercial kitchen.

Although the initial capital cost is often more than that for an integral units, remote units are usually much more efficient in the long run.

With a remote refrigeration unit the compressor and the other elements that can be hot and noisy are located away from the cold room its self, and is connected by insulated pipes that carry the heat away from the unit. This not only means that the heat is taken away from the unit its self to increase efficiency , but noise around the unit is also reduced; prefect for a commercial kitchen where communication is essential during food service times.

Remote units are however more complex to install, and will usually require a site survey and a specialist engineer to install the unit.

If you're not sure whether a remote refrigeration unit is right for you, give our sales team a call on 01229 48000 for some friendly and helpful advice on our wide range of cold rooms.

commercial_refrigeration-meat_fish_chill.description:
Here at Caterkwik we sell a range of specialised display refrigerators, designed especially for fish.

Within the commercial business presentation can be everything. Our fresh fish serve overs are designed specifically to optimise the showcasing of your fresh fish items whilst keeping them fresh and safe.

All our fish display counters are easy clean ensuring that you can keep to health and safety regulations. Health and Safety regulations are tough, and these refrigerated fish displays help you to easily comply with the regulations whilst still providing you with the means to display your fish attractively and practically.

These fresh fish display counters are ideal for use within supermarkets, delis, restaurants & fishmongers.

Here at Caterkwik we sell a range of specialised storage refrigerators, designed especially for fish.

A fish keeper can be an essential asset when a business deals with a large selection of meat and fish dishes. By providing ideal environment for wet fish our fish fridges make sure that the fish is kept without spoiling the product. A conventional catering fridge uses a fan to assist the cooling process this in turn tends to dry fish out and spoil quality. Fish keepers are designed to have slow moving circulation within the cooling process which does not dry the fish out keeping them fresher for longer.

Fresh Fish give off ammonia - lots of it! Another benefit of using a purpose built fresh fish keeper is that they are made with a coated coil (cooling element). Within standard fridges the coil (cooling element) when used for keeping fish will corrode due to the high ammonia vapor. With the knowledge of this fish fridges are built with coils that have a coating on them that are resistant to these high levels of ammonia vapor. This prolongs the life of the machines and less chance of any breakages.

With different compartments and draws you are able to keep the fish separate. These draws come with their own drain plates to ensure excess fluid drains away keeping fish fresher and also means that no cross contamination between the draws is enabled. These drain plates can be removed and cleaned making it easier to comply with health and safety regulations. Health and Safety regulations are tough, and these units help you to easily comply with said regulations whist still providing you with the means to store your fish in an efficient and practical way. Ideal for any commercial kitchen!

Need help choosing your fish keeper - just give our sales team a call on 01229 480001 and they will be happy to help.

Here for all your commercial refrigeration needs if you cannot see what you are looking for call us today and a member of our team will be happy to help.

Climate Classes Explained.

Climate Class 3 : Maximum ambient temperature of 25°C with 60% RH*

Climate Class 4 : Maximum ambient temperature of 30°C with 55% RH*

Climate Class 5 : Maximum ambient temperature of 40°C with 40% RH*

SN Class : Ambient operating temperature between +10° and +32°C .

N Class : Ambient operating temperature between +16° and +32°C .

ST Class : Ambient operating temperature between +18° and +38°C .

Stick blenders are a necessity to the commercial kitchen. A commercial hand blender is able to simplify many processes in a professional kitchen. They are designed to mix and blend large amounts of food, including soups, sauces, batters, mayonnaise, gravies and many more can quickly and easily be produced to save you valuable time.

Immersion blenders are much more efficient than preparing by hand. Unlike kitchen or bar blenders, a hand blender's main advantage is their portability which allows the stick blender to be taken to its ingredients rather than the other way around.

Where gas cooking appliances are used, all extraction systems in commercial catering establishments must have a gas interlocking system in place to comply with BS6173 and IGEM/UP/19, and this should be installed by a qualified gas engineer. Gas interlock systems prevent the gas supply from being turned on until ventilation is fully operational. Gas interlock systems such as the Merlin CT1200S use an air pressure sensor which detects when the canopy is working correctly with sufficient air flow. Once this is achieved the gas solenoid valve will open and cooking appliances can be used.

Here at Cater-Kwik we are able to offer a variety of gas interlock systems to suit the needs of any professional kitchen. We are also able to offer expert impartial advice, site surveys, design and installation for commercial extraction systems. If you are in any doubt as to your gas interlocking or extraction requirements please don't hesitate to contact our team on 01229 480001.

If you need any help or guidance, please complete the short questionnaire here . One of our commercial extraction experts will review and get in touch.

For detailed information and guidelines on ventilation and gas interlocking systems in commercial kitchens, please refer to this recognized HSE Kitchen Ventilation Document .

If you can't find what you are looking for please get in touch our fabricators can build to your specifications at very competitive prices.

Air pressure differential switches can be used to detect disruption in air flow and automatically shut off the gas supply as part of a gas interlock system. Current sensors can be used as an alternative to air pressure differential switches in commercial gas interlock systems to monitor the air current from extraction fans. Gas detectors are used to monitor emissions such as the build up of carbon dioxide or natural gas, and can be used as part of an interlock system to trigger an audible alarm and isolate the gas solenoid valve.

If you are in any doubt as to your gas interlocking or extraction requirements, please click here to fill out our quick & easy questionnaire. Once completed, this will be sent to our in house commercial extraction experts to determine which system is best to suit your needs. We will then be able to contact you with more accurate details and prices of what you require.

Gas interlocking systems that utilise current sensing switches work by monitoring the flow of electricity to the extraction fan system. With the fan system not in use the switch detects the drop in amperage and does not allow the flow of gas to the appliances through the installed gas solenoid valves.

Current sensing switches are either able to monitor 1 individual fan, or 2 fans simultaneously. They can also be finely tuned, allowing the user to set high and low current ranges depending on the power demands of the fan system.

As an alternative to air pressure differential switches, current sensing systems rely on zero moving parts to function and are a great choice for a new installation. Merlin offer a number of options to choose from, all of which integrate seamlessly into their interlocking panels.

Gas interlocking systems that make use of air pressure differential switches work by detecting disruption in the flow of air through the extraction ducting, signified as a change in air pressure. With a drop in air pressure, the switch then cuts off the supply to all gas solenoid valves.

Air pressure differential switches are supplied with sufficient ducting tube to be able to reach the desired location along the extraction system. As well as this, they feature adjustable sensitivities designed to work with different fan types.

Baffle filters used in extraction canopies provide the perfect alternative to mesh grease filters.

Baffle filters are designed to allow grease and grime to collect within the fins and drip into either a grease tray or long collection run. Most canopies are installed with a drainage tap to allow for the emptying and cleaning of the system whenever it is required.

Made of high grade corrosion resistant stainless steel, baffle filters are must have for your commercial extraction system.

Gas detectors are used to monitor emissions and the build up of both carbon monoxide and carbon dioxide, as well as natural gas and LPG leaks.

Used in conjunction with Merlin interlock panels, these detectors provide the user with an added layer of safety. Unlike domestic gas monitoring alarms, Merlin commercial gas detectors have added security and fail-safe measures ensuring seamless function in day to day use. Merlin's 3000S Demand Control Interlocking system solves the problem of potentially harmful gasses automatically, by increasing or decreasing the fan RPM depending on gas levels within the kitchen.

The dangers that the build up of these gasses present can be both detrimental to the running of your kitchen as well as potentially life threatening. Carbon monoxide is one of the more dangerous gasses which can accumulate in a kitchen that makes use of solid fuel appliances. These fuels if left to smoulder can produce the gas over time. The dangers this can present are build ups occurring when a business is closed, and upon start of service, individuals being presented with a potentially lethal environment.

Different detectors require installation at different heights, due to varying density of the gasses present.

Natural Gas/Methane (NG/CH4) - 300mm (1ft) from ceiling.

Liquid Petroleum Gas (LPG) - 300mm (1ft) from ground level.

Carbon Monoxide (CO) - 1700mm (5ft 6") from ground level. (BREATHING ZONE)

Carbon Dioxide (CO2) - 1700mm (5ft 6") from ground level. (BREATHING ZONE)

Hydrogen (H2) - 300mm (1ft) from ceiling.

dishwashers-condensate.description:
In a kitchen moisture is part of the working day. Just cooking food releases moisture into the environment making the air more humid.

When you introduce ware washing solutions into a catering environment the moisture levels increase dramatically, and in a kitchen that's not always good for food or the staff.

Condensate hoods are designed to manage and expel excess moisture produced by high steam output equipment like dishwashers, combination ovens and atmospheric steamers.

Fitted above equipment, these canopies allow steam laden air ti be safely captured.

They are fitted with sloped condensation plate, which on contact with steam turns it into water and then directs it into a drain off, keeping it out of the air and reducing overall environmental humidity.

The results is less humidity, drier surfaces and a safer and more comfortable working environment.

Reverse osmosis is the optimum way of getting the perfect wash water. The process uses pressurised water that passes through a semi-permeable membrane to remove all unwanted minerals & ions. Minerals in the water can cause glasses & utensils to become dull & have small streaks & residue. Even with a water softener glasses can become dull over time. Reverse osmosis is the ideal solution for businesses that want to have that perfect shine. It also saves costs as staff spend less time having to polish to make them presentable again. Finally, reverse osmosis prevents limescale from entering your machine to help with life expectancy & reduce engineering bills.

GreasePak is a unique, automatic drain dosing system specifically designed to address the drainage problems found in commercial kitchens. 10 YEARS ON AND STILL THE BEST!

Winner of "Excellence in Catering Equipment & Supplies Awards 2006"

Commercial kitchens naturally discharge high levels of fats, oils & greases (FOGs) into the drains. This can result in slow drains & blockages which releases bad odours & create unacceptable health & hygiene hazards in the kitchen. The traditional solution involves the use of bulky, expensive grease traps which take up valuable space & can be difficult to clean. Grease traps need emptying & managing which rarely happens. Lack of maintenance leaves a foul water reservoir, which quickly becomes rancid & odorous attracting insects & vermin - cleaning grease traps is a nasty job which can result in kitchen contamination.

Alternative dosing units rely on large drums of single strain chemical with a mechanical pump. Greasepak's highly develeloped & powerful Bio-Enzymatic solution deals with fats, oil & grease leaving staff free to run the kitchen. Maintains free running drains. Helps foodservice operators meet with legislative demands.

Requires no water or electrical connections. An effective environmentally friendly solution. BBA Approved.

The perfect coffee should be between 80-120 PPM, however if you leave water at this hardness you sacrifice the longevity of your appliance. Claris Ultra filters locks water hardness to between these figures ensuring that you have the hardness for taste but it doesn’t leave scale deposits when heated.

If you live in a hard water area ( Click here for hard water map ), you will require a Claris Ultra Filtration Kit.

If you live in a soft water area ( Click here for hard water map ), the water should still be treated for taste and odour. This is due to all UK mains water having added chlorine in it, which can severely affect the taste of food & drink.

sparesaccesories-commercial-gas-hoses.description:
High specification, heavy duty commercial gas hoses with restraining cables.

Beware of cheap inferior quality hoses .

BTU Capacities

Referring to the chart below, the BTU Capacities of Both Caterquip & Dormont gas hoses are shown.

These capacities were determined under the test conditions specified in BS669 part 2 1997.

They are for braided & unbraided gas hoses fitted with standard quick-disconnect (QD) fittings or Safety Quik™.

Correct gas hose installation

When installing your commercial gas hose, positioning is crucial for both the integrity and function of the hose.

• The quick-disconnect (QD) end must be at the supply end.

• Allow the hose to form 1 natural loop. There should be no sharp bends, crimps or twists.

• Ensure the hose is not touching the floor - if this is an issue, you should consider a shorter length hose.

• The restraining chain should be slightly shorter than the hose. Doing so correctly prevents over-extending of the gas hose.

The restrainer should NOT be attached to either the gas supply or gas hose itself. It should be securely anchored in the wall.

commercial_gas_interlock_systems.description:
Where gas cooking appliances are used, all extraction systems in commercial catering establishments must have a gas interlocking system in place to comply with BS6173 and IGEM/UP/19, and this should be installed by a qualified gas engineer. Gas interlock systems prevent the gas supply from being turned on until ventilation is fully operational. Gas interlock systems such as the Merlin CT1200S use an air pressure sensor which detects when the canopy is working correctly with sufficient air flow. Once this is achieved the gas solenoid valve will open and cooking appliances can be used.

Here at Cater-Kwik we are able to offer a variety of gas interlock systems to suit the needs of any professional kitchen. We are also able to offer expert impartial advice, site surveys, design and installation for commercial extraction systems. If you are in any doubt as to your gas interlocking or extraction requirements please don't hesitate to contact our team on 01229 480001.

If you need any help or guidance, please complete the short questionnaire here . One of our commercial extraction experts will review and get in touch.

For detailed information and guidelines on ventilation and gas interlocking systems in commercial kitchens, please refer to this recognized HSE Kitchen Ventilation Document .

extraction-systems-extraction-canopies.description:
Extraction systems are built around a canopy system. A large, overhead structure in which the ducting is connected. Extraction canopies are made in a vast number of sizes, all dependant on what equipment is used. While an extraction canopy system is not technically required when using solely electrical appliances, they are a recommended item due to the more comfortable working environment they produce.

When gas appliances are installed in the kitchen, certain canopy sizes must be adhered to. Overhangs on both the sides and front of the appliance must be 300mm minimum. (An oven with a depth of 800mm would require a minimum canopy depth of 1100mm. 1200mm would be a preferred depth, to account for gas connections behind the oven).
